Toy Story 5 is Actually a ReBoot Sequel

short // Jul 29, 2026

Watch on YouTube

Everybody gives Pixar's Toy Story the credit for being the first 3D cartoon. It wasn't. Not even close. Something beat it by more than a year, and the wild part is that it's secretly the same story, all the way up to Toy Story 5.

ReBoot beat Toy Story by over a year

ReBoot premiered in September 1994, a Canadian show that aired Saturday mornings on YTV and ABC. It was the first fully computer-animated TV series ever made. Toy Story didn't hit theaters until November 1995. Pixar got the first CGI feature film, but ReBoot got there first.

Mainframe and the User

Inside a computer lives a city called Mainframe. Every time a kid loads up a game, it drops on that city like a bomb.

Because to everybody in Mainframe, the kid at the keyboard is a god. They call him the User, and they can't agree on him:

  • Some look up to him.
  • Some blame him for the viruses.
  • Some think he isn't even real, just a story somebody made up to keep everybody in line.

Andy's toys live by the same rules

Swap the computer for a kid's bedroom and you've got Toy Story. Don't move. Don't get seen. Live for the kid. And just like the Mainframe doubters, Buzz spends the whole first movie refusing to believe he's a toy at all.

Where the two stories split

This is where ReBoot goes darker. In Mainframe, the User drops a game, loads himself in as a character, and the programs have to beat him. If he wins, everyone caught in that game gets wiped out. If he loses, they get to see another day.

Same kind of god. Way higher price.

When the kids grew up, both worlds paid for it

Andy trades his toys for camp, a cell phone and friends, then college and adulthood.

The User moves on to darker games, and he wins one. It costs Enzo, Mainframe's wide-eyed kid, his eye and his innocence. He comes back as Matrix, and the whole system has to crash and reboot just to survive.

Two worlds abandoned by gods who never knew they existed

Then both gods leave.

Andy donates his toys to Bonnie, and Woody has to figure out life without him. In ReBoot, by the final two episodes the User's keyboard is just dead. Mainframe goes dark for nearly 20 years, until the 2018 sequel, ReBoot: The Guardian Code, reveals him as a grown man-child buried under ReBoot merch in his mom's basement.

Two worlds, abandoned by gods who never knew they existed.

The wildest part is what happened in real life

The story is wild. Reality is wilder.

Toy Story got five movies and billions at the box office. ReBoot got the opposite. The House of Mouse dropped it as soon as Disney bought ABC. YTV and Toonami kept it alive for more seasons until the money ran dry, and Season 4 got cut down to eight episodes.

So they rewrote the ending into a cliffhanger on purpose. Megabyte wins. Game over.

This show spent seven years telling a story about a world left behind by its god, and then it became one. The creator still holds the true ending, in case he ever gets to finish it.

Both worlds saved themselves

Andy didn't come to that incinerator in Toy Story 3. Mainframe fought Megabyte with nobody at the keyboard. In both worlds, when it counted most, the god wasn't there, so they saved themselves.

Toy Story 5 brings it full circle

In Toy Story 5, the toys finally clash with technology itself, going up against tech like Lilypad, a tablet that would fit right in inside Mainframe. By the end, they learn how to coexist.

So the next time some jabroni calls Toy Story 5 just another sequel, tell them it's a crossover 30 years in the making.

Quick answers

Was Toy Story the first 3D cartoon? No. ReBoot premiered in September 1994 as the first fully computer-animated TV series, more than a year before Toy Story (November 1995), which was the first fully computer-animated feature film.

What is ReBoot about? It's set in Mainframe, a city inside a computer. When the User loads a game, the programs have to beat him inside it, or everyone caught in the game gets wiped out.

Who is the User in ReBoot? The person at the keyboard. To the people of Mainframe he's a god. Some worship him, some blame him, and some don't believe he's real.

Why did ReBoot end on a cliffhanger? The money ran out. Season 4 was cut to eight episodes, so the ending was rewritten into a cliffhanger on purpose, with Megabyte winning.

Is there a ReBoot sequel? Yes. ReBoot: The Guardian Code came out in 2018.

What is Toy Story 5 about? Toys versus tech. The toys clash with technology like Lilypad, a tablet, and learn to coexist with it.

Your turn

Did you grow up on ReBoot, Toy Story, or both? Is Toy Story 5 secretly a ReBoot sequel, or am I reaching? Tell me in the comments. Follow, or get rebooted.
